title: Space Tech Briefing — August 27, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and welcome to your daily dose of cosmic updates! This is your Space Technology Briefing, live on this exciting Thursday, August 27, 2026. We're soaring through the latest in orbit and beyond, and today, we've got some incredible feats of human endeavor in low Earth orbit to recap!

As we look up to the stars, we're celebrating a remarkable series of spacewalks that have truly captured our attention. European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot has been making history, not once, not twice, but three times in just three weeks!

Let's rewind just a moment. On August 25th, Sophie Adenot completed her *second* spacewalk, marking a significant milestone. She became the very first European woman to achieve two Extravehicular Activities, or EVAs, to her name. During that mission, alongside her crewmate Anil Menon, their primary objective was precise: they successfully installed a brand-new antenna on the International Space Station, replacing one they had previously dismantled on August 19th. Precision work in the vacuum of space!

And the action didn't stop there! Just yesterday, August 26th, Sophie Adenot was back outside the ISS for her *third* spacewalk in three weeks. This time, she was in excellent company, paired with American astronaut Jessica Meir. Their mission? Crucial maintenance work on the International Space Station, ensuring our orbital outpost remains in peak condition. It's an incredible testament to the dedication and skill of our astronauts, performing complex tasks hundreds of kilometers above us.

What an extraordinary few weeks for Sophie Adenot and the entire ISS crew! These spacewalks are vital for keeping the station operational and pushing the boundaries of human presence in space.

That's all for your morning space briefing on this August 27, 2026. Keep looking up, stay curious, and we'll catch you next time for more thrilling updates from the final frontier. Have a stellar day!
